PengyOS 26.11.6 - SSH can accept a password, if you choose it. Keys only stays the default.

Server and Desktop (all four editions):
- **SSH password logins, opt-in.** PengyOS's SSH accepts keys only, and that stays
  the default. Someone who has never made an SSH key could not get into a new
  machine at all. Now the installers ask:
  - the console installer has an **SSH login** page: *Keys only* (recommended) or
    *Keys or password*;
  - the Desktop installer has an **Allow SSH logins with a password** switch on
    its account screen.

  Both warn that a password can be guessed by anyone who can reach the machine.
  root never logs in with a password over SSH, either way.
- **`pengyos-ssh-password`** changes it on an installed machine:
  - `sudo pengyos-ssh-password on` lets SSH accept passwords;
  - `sudo pengyos-ssh-password off` goes back to keys only (it refuses until some
    account has a key, so nobody is locked out);
  - `pengyos-ssh-password` shows which is on and how to set up a key: `ssh-keygen`,
    then `ssh-copy-id` (or one PowerShell line on Windows).

  While passwords are on, every login shows a reminder, and an address that keeps
  getting the password wrong waits longer between tries.

Installer fix:
- The line-by-line console installer skipped the SSH page after "Enter to skip
  Wi-Fi", so no key was asked for. It asks again now.

Editions rebuilt: all five, incrementally (the Server and Desktop overlays, the
installers and the install sticks).
Verified: every image boot-checked under QEMU before signing.
